title: Dedicated Pool On-call Simulations & Autoscale Contingency Plan
creator: Priya Desai
description: Goal: Reduce mean time to recovery (MTTR) for dedicated-pool autoscale failures by running quarterly on-call simulations, validating automated fallback paths (warm pools, model-variant routing), and publishing a tested contingency runbook with playbook checks. This ticket coordinates PM, SRE, and runtime engineering work to design, execute, and iterate on a simulation program that surfaces hidden failure modes in autoscale and warm-pool behaviors.
acceptance_criteria: One full simulation run executed against a staging dedicated pool that mimics 3x normal traffic burst and 50% GPU allocation loss
Runbook updated with step-by-step recovery actions, roles, and escalation matrix and validated by SRE during dry-run
Three measurable telemetry alerts (latency, queue-length, model-fallback rate) have thresholded playbook triggers and are hooked into pager routes
Post-simulation retrospective with action items assigned to ENG/Runtime/Console teams and SLA for fixes (P0 within 2 weeks, P1 within 6 weeks)
Automated canary that exercises fallback routing is merged to main and has a smoke test green on staging
milestones: Design simulation scenarios and failure injections — 2026-02-25
Build orchestration job and safe staging harness — 2026-03-05
Merge automated fallback canary and smoke run — 2026-03-24
deliverables: Contingency runbook (Confluence) with play-by-play and run-checklist
Simulation harness (k8s job + load generator) in infra repo with docs
Dashboard tile and alerts for latency/queue/fallback-rate in Grafana
PR with fallback-canary automation and smoke tests
Retrospective notes and prioritized backlog of fixes
risks: Staging environment may not faithfully reproduce production queueing behavior (workload skew)
Simulation could trigger customer-impacting cascades if accidentally targeted at prod; safety gating must be airtight
Dependency on ENG-11834 (KV-cache eviction fix) to make fallback deterministic
Insufficient on-call bandwidth during week of simulation causing delayed triage
comments: 2026-02-19 — Priya: Kickoff meeting notes posted. Agreed to focus first sim on a 50% GPU loss + sudden 3x request burst. Action: ENG to provide safe staging target by 2026-02-25.
2026-02-26 — Zara: Staging harness prototype is ready; it uses a sidecar load generator that can replay recorded traffic shapes. Need a gating flag to ensure no cross-tenant blast radius.
2026-03-02 — Evan: Pager rotations aligned; SRE will own the dry-run weekend window. Added alert thresholds to testing Grafana panel and mapped to on-call paging rules.

2026-03-08 — Marco: Simulation orchestration job merged to infra staging branch (PR #3921). Noted intermittent KV-cache eviction observed during internal priming runs — opening ENG dependency ENG-20291.

2026-03-10 — Simulation run (dry-run) executed; fallback routing engaged successfully but fallback rate was slower than SLA (median failover 18s vs target 8s). Collecting logs and trace spans; postmortem scheduled 2026-03-11.

2026-03-11 — Postmortem summary: root cause traced to slow model-variant cold-start path and queue-starvation under prioritization policy. Action items: optimize cold-start path (ENG-20722), add short-lived prewarm for critical models, adjust queue_priority heuristic. Assigned owners and SLAs.

2026-03-12 — Priya: Runbook draft updated with escalation matrix and checklist. Requesting review from Runtime and SRE. Next: merge fallback canary automation and schedule the validated production-safe simulation in next cycle.
